builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
summary: Replaces ad-hoc interpretation of scattered research artifacts—raw code, papers, and supplementary materials—with a structured reproducibility package comprising refined codebase, environment specifications, experiment launchers, and documented procedures. Costs include an initial agent-driven construction phase to generate the refined artifacts and ongoing maintenance to keep them synchronized with upstream changes. Failure modes include artifacts becoming outdated as underlying libraries evolve, propagation of errors if the initial artifact generation contains subtle inaccuracies, and residual dependence on agent capability for edge cases not covered by the standardized components.
rationale: Standardizing execution knowledge into persistent artifacts reduces API expenditure by 19.7% and lowers variance in reproduction success across models, making it immediately deployable for engineers relying on third-party APIs without cluster infrastructure.
technique: Standardized Reproducibility Artifacts via Agent Workflow

claims.statement: Replaces ad-hoc interpretation of scattered research artifacts—raw code, papers, and supplementary materials—with a structured reproducibility package comprising refined codebase, environment specifications, experiment launchers, and documented procedures. Costs include an initial agent-driven construction phase to generate the refined artifacts and ongoing maintenance to keep them synchronized with upstream changes. Failure modes include artifacts becoming outdated as underlying libraries evolve, propagation of errors if the initial artifact generation contains subtle inaccuracies, and residual dependence on agent capability for edge cases not covered by the standardized components.
Across four evaluated models, refined artifacts reduce downstream API spending by 19.7% on average while raising mean reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6%.
